about.title: The person behind World History Chronicle
about.lead: We believe history is more than dates. It is how people made decisions, collided and left traces. This project exists to make learning history more approachable, searchable and trustworthy.
about.missionText: To create an open historical encyclopedia that prioritises Vietnam while always placing it in regional and global context; written for general readers but respectful of scholarly standards.
storyParagraphs: World History Chronicle began with a simple question: why do many people know the major events but struggle to picture where they happened, when, and how they connect?
We chose to combine timelines, maps and short sourced articles. Each event sits beside others from the same era so readers can sense the rhythm of history.
The project was bilingual from the start, ready for mobile applications and open to community contributions. We see it as a growing product, not a closed book.

values.title: Accuracy first
values.text: When the evidence is not yet firm, we state the limits instead of presenting a claim as absolute fact.

values.title: Context over lists
values.text: Each article tries to answer why an event happened, who was affected and how long the consequences lasted.

values.title: Respect for readers
values.text: Clear language, no sensationalism, and no turning history into cheap entertainment.

methodParagraphs: Every draft is checked against at least two independent sources where possible. Ancient milestones are clearly separated into legend, historical record and archaeological evidence.
Illustrations are currently produced by our design team; we do not use images with unclear copyright. When archival images are added, their source and licence are stated.
Reader contributions are reviewed before publication. Sending a contribution does not guarantee that it will be published.
about.teamSubtitle: One person is responsible for all of the encyclopedia's content, design and engineering, following transparent editorial principles and source checking.

team.name: Do Tien Phat
team.bio: Runs the whole encyclopedia: content structure and voice, source checking for both Vietnamese and world history, the reading experience, maps, data and secure infrastructure.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.subtitle: Five questions about how we build content, verify sources and handle contributions.

items.question: What does this website offer?
items.answer: World History Chronicle is a bilingual history encyclopedia that prioritises Vietnam and places events in a global context. Each event includes a summary, a multi-paragraph article, a map location, keywords and links to related events.

items.question: Is the content verified?
items.answer: We compare historical sources, museums and open encyclopedias, preferring at least two independent sources where possible. For ancient milestones, articles clearly separate legend, record and archaeological evidence. Content may still contain errors and is always open to correction.

items.question: How can I contribute materials?
items.answer: Use the Contribute page to send your name, email, details and a related topic. The editorial team will read it, check the sources and contact you if more information is needed. Submission does not guarantee publication.

items.question: Does the site use maps and external data?
items.answer: The map draws its own coastlines, land borders and place names from the public Natural Earth dataset shipped with the site, so no third-party tile server is contacted while you browse. The Wider perspective section may retrieve a summary from Wikipedia and always states the source. If an external service is unavailable, the main article still displays normally.

items.question: Is there an English version and a mobile app?
items.answer: The entire interface and all event content are available in Vietnamese and English. The application programming interface is designed separately so it can serve Android and iOS applications in the future, but no mobile app has been released yet.

faq.moreText: Send a question or topic suggestion to the editorial team. We read every message.

privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.intro: This policy explains what we collect, why we collect it, how we protect it and what rights you have. We try to collect only what is genuinely necessary to run the encyclopedia.

sections.title: Data controller and contact point
paragraphs: {owner} operates this website and is the party that decides the purposes and means of processing the personal data described in this policy.

Requests about personal data and complaints go to sukytoancau@gmail.com, or through the Contribute page. Please state the name you used when contributing and what you would like us to do, so that we can verify the request.

sections.title: Data we collect
paragraphs: When you send a contribution we receive your name, email address, contribution details and chosen topic. Email addresses are encrypted before being stored in the database.

The server records a minimal amount of technical data such as request time and network address. The network address is hashed with a secret key to prevent spam; we do not store the original address for this purpose.
If you agree, Google Analytics is used to understand how people read articles. You can decline and the site remains fully functional.

sections.title: How we use data
paragraphs: We use contribution data to contact you, verify information and add content; we use technical data to detect abuse, protect the system and improve the reading experience.
We do not sell personal data and we do not use your email address for advertising.

sections.title: How we protect data
paragraphs: Email addresses in contributions are encrypted with an application key. Administrator passwords are stored only as hashes produced by a dedicated algorithm.
The Postgres database in deployed environments enables row-level security: the public may read events and submit contributions but may not read other people's contributions.
The website applies security headers, submission rate limits, input validation and the principle of least privilege for service accounts.

sections.title: Retention
paragraphs: Contributions are kept until processed and for no more than 24 months, unless a longer period is needed to resolve a dispute or required by law.
Analytics data is aggregated and retained according to the analytics provider's terms.

sections.title: Third-party services
paragraphs: The map does not call any third-party tile server: coastlines, land borders and place names ship inside the page. Opening the map connects to no map service and does not expose your network address.
The Wider perspective section calls the Wikipedia API. We do not send your personal information in these requests.
Google Analytics loads only after you agree. We do not configure advertising data sharing.

sections.title: Cookies and local storage
paragraphs: Technical cookies remember your language and theme choices. Your analytics choice and saved events are kept in your browser's local storage.
You can clear cookies and local data at any time in your browser settings.

sections.title: Your rights
paragraphs: You may request access to, correction of or deletion of personal information you have sent, withdraw analytics consent and object to processing.
To do so, send a request through the Contribute page stating what you would like us to do. We may need to verify the request first.

sections.title: Contact and response deadlines
paragraphs: Send questions about this policy to sukytoancau@gmail.com or use the Contribute page. We reply and guide you through the procedure within two working days of receiving a request.

Processing deadlines follow Article 5 of Decree 356/2025/ND-CP: access, correction or provision of data within 10 days, or 15 days when the processing party or a third party must be involved; withdrawal of consent, restriction of or objection to processing within 15 days, or 20 days when the processing party must be asked to stop processing; erasure within 20 days, or 30 days when the processing party or a third party must be involved.

We extend a deadline once at most and only when the request is genuinely complex: up to 10 extra days for access and correction, 15 for withdrawal and objection, 20 for erasure. When we extend, we tell you why.
The policy may be updated when our practices change. The revision date is always shown at the top.
